newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Japan PM says remarks on U.S. bonds misunderstood.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM says remarks on U.S. bonds misunderstood.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said remarks he made on Monday regarding Tokyo's huge interests in U.S. Treasuries had been misunderstood, a European Union source said on Wednesday.
The EU source said Hashimoto had told leaders at a Japan-EU summit in The Hague that comments he made regarding Japanese ownership of U.S. government bonds had been "unskilled".
"There was not much discussion on the issue," the source told Reuters. "He said he had been misunderstood...perhaps unskilled."

Hashimoto's comments, seen by some analysts as a veiled warning to the U.S. not to criticise Japan's growing trade surplus, sent shivers through financial markets amid concern that Tokyo might begin selling U.S. bonds.
Hashimoto said on Monday that in the past Japan had been tempted to sell some of its Treasuries but had not done so.
"I hope the U.S. will engage in efforts and in cooperation to maintain exchange stability so we will not succumb to the temptation ... and switch to gold," he said.
Japanese officials have since tried to play down his remarks.

During the EU-Japan summit, Hashimoto met Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok -- whose country currently holds the rotating EU presidency -- European Commission President Jacques Santer and EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan.
They discussed trade and investment issues as well as ways to increase political links.
